bug_semantics: SQLE ships a compile-time JWT HMAC secret of the literal string "secret". The advisory sink is sqle/utils/jwt.go JWTSecretKey (`var JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret")`). ParseAuditPlanName and GetUserNameFromJWTToken use that global as the HS256 key, so anyone who knows the default can forge tokens (including admin uid 700200) against installs that never override the key. GHSA-43h9-hc38-qph5 / CVE-2025-15107 (CWE-321/CWE-798) is reviewed and not withdrawn; issue actiontech/sqle#3186 remains open on milestone v4.2607.0 with no linked closing PR. HEAD still contains the hardcoded initializer; GHSA lists no first_patched_version.
flaw_origin: The hardcoded JWT secret was first written in 70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0 ("add jwt auth for api", 2021-02-26, author/committer Sun Jian). That commit created sqle/api/controller/auth_v1.go with `const JWTSecret = "secret"` and signed login tokens via `token.SignedString([]byte(JWTSecret))`, and wired echo JWT middleware in sqle/api/app.go to `[]byte(controller.JWTSecret)`. Parent 70757e49453c461398cf61515a94fd116b8a96d7 has neither auth_v1.go nor any JWTSecret/`[]byte("secret")` Go hit. Later commits only moved or renamed the same default: ee756efd copied it into v1/auth.go; e0604a3e extracted `const JWTSecret = "secret"` into new sqle/utils/jwt.go; 866f1fc4 pointed ParseAuditPlanName at the AES SecretKey while leaving the const in place; d81fd4a1 restored `var JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret")` for upgrade compatibility. Blame of today's jwt.go:9 lands on that restore, which is not a first-write BIC because the parent tree still had `const JWTSecret = "secret"`.

potential_fix.approach: Remove the compile-time default HMAC key. JWTSecretKey must be initialized only from a deployment-unique secret_key (config/env); refuse to start if that secret is empty or still the literal "secret". Rotate any tokens previously signed with the default and stop shipping vendor defaultDMSToken-style credentials.
potential_fix.rationale: Without a globally known default, remote attackers cannot mint valid HS256 JWTs from public source. Fail-closed startup prevents the current default-on-deploy path described in issue #3186.
